Subject: Recap & next steps 

PO vs Card procurement 

Hi Ari - thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

- Procurement policy: you mentioned AP prefers POs for vendors over a company card for purchases > $5k.
- Vendor onboarding: FinOpsCo needs a vendor profile + W9 and the standard vendor-form for marketplace/SaaS vendors.
- Commercial path: you indicated possibility of marketplace procurement (AWS Marketplace) but AP needs confirmation whether Redwood is listed / able to accept marketplace invoices.

Next steps I suggest:
1) I'll send an itemized pricing estimate and the vendor onboarding form for your AP team. (Attached: Redwood-pricing-estimate-20270112.pdf; vendor-onboarding-form-FinOpsCo.xlsx)
2) Can you confirm the primary procurement contact (name + email) I should loop in?
3) If AP requires a PO, what is your expected lead time for PO issuance and any required PO fields (company legal name, tax id, billing address, contact)?

I'm looping Marissa (our finance lead) to help answer any questions on invoicing and to confirm whether we can support marketplace billing or need a direct invoice/PO.

Thanks - talk soon.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

PO vs Card procurement

Thanks Lauren - appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from AP side:

- Confirmed: our AP policy requires a PO for any vendor commitment that will be invoiced and paid on Net terms. Cards are allowed for one-off purchases under $5k but anything recurring or multi-month needs a PO.
- Vendor onboarding: procurement@finopsco.com handles vendor profile creation. They need the vendor-form completed + W9 and a primary finance contact.
- Marketplace: we prefer to buy via AWS Marketplace when available because billing goes on our marketplace contract; however, we cannot use Marketplace for vendors who are not listed or who require custom legal terms.

Action items on our side:
- I'll introduce you to the procurement owner, Kelly Ramos (procurement@finopsco.com), who will own the vendor profile.
- We typically take 7-10 business days from receipt of a fully completed vendor-form to issue a PO. If legal review is required, add 5-7 business days.

Cc'ing Kelly now (procurement@finopsco.com) - Kelly, Lauren is our Redwood contact. Please advise on the vendor-form and any additional fields you need on the PO.

Best,
Ari
Senior Product Manager | FinOpsCo
ari.patel@finopsco.com

Hi all - quick finance note to keep things moving:

- We reviewed the pricing estimate and the PO line items Lauren included look good.
- If you plan to use AWS Marketplace, please note we currently support subscription billing via AWS Marketplace for our hosted offering - I can confirm the AWS product listing ID if needed. Marketplace purchases will appear on your regular AWS bill and do not require a separate PO to be sent to us, but your internal AP may still need to record a marketplace order number.
- If FinOpsCo prefers a direct PO, we can accept PO invoicing on Net30. Once we receive the PO, we'll generate invoices monthly.

Kelly / procurement@finopsco.com: if you want the AWS listing ID or a formal quote in DocuSign for signature, let me know and I'll share the link.
